text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easier for others to use. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names, such as /users or /orders. Use the right HTTP methods, like GET to read data and POST to create it. Always return proper status codes so clients know what happened—for example, 200 for success and 404 when something is missing. Good documentation is essential, because it explains how each endpoint works. Finally, use versioning, such as /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Following these practices keeps your API reliable and easy to maintain.
